item.title: Ringing in the Jewish new year with a twist on a Rosh Hashanah classic
item.description: Pati Jinich is a renowned chef and cookbook author. She was born in Mexico to a Jewish family, and her marzipan-stuffed challah bread blends her cultures in an exciting and delicious way.

item.description: Reporting over so-called "the Great Firewall," a journalist details how to report for a global audience from Beijing despite tight obstacles imposed by the government.

item.title: She left Canada to support ISIS. Now she's back and trying to rebuild a life
item.description: A young Canadian mother shares her memories of being an ISIS bride, and her harrowing escape from the extremist group.

item.title: REMEMBERING LOVED ONES KILLED IN UNITED 93 CRASH
item.description: On September 11, 2001 Lori Guadagno lost her brother on flight United 93. 25 years later, the crash site is a place where she feels a sense of connection that she can't find anywhere else.

item.title: Cost of living has gone up 3.4% in the last year
item.description: A new report shows the cost of living in August was up 3.4% from a year ago. Investors think stubborn inflation makes it more likely that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week.

item.title: Ethics watchdogs await RFK Jr.'s financial report
item.description: Health Secretary RFK Jr.'s annual financial disclosure is late. When it posts, the public could learn how much he has earned from a vaccine-related lawsuit against Merck, which RFK now regulates.

item.title: The other side of 9/11: Afghans reckon with America's long shadow
item.description: It's been nearly 25 years since the start of the U.S- led invasion of Afghanistan. NPR returns to Kabul to see how Afghans, now back under Taliban rule, are coping with the legacy of that 20 year war.
